key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implant performance depends on integrating load-bearing geometry with durable, bone-integrating biomaterial interfaces.
engineering_relevance: Design must balance gait-dependent stresses and micromotion with coating integrity, fatigue resistance, and long-term biological fixation.
method: Systematic review of implant geometry, gait-phase finite element analysis, and biomaterial interfaces.
Assessment of graded Ti–hydroxyapatite architectures and in-vivo osseointegration evidence.
Quantitative trend analysis of evidence maturity and clinical translation readiness.
evidence_signal: The analysis covered 34 direct-contribution papers and 32 empirical studies, with more than half of empirical evidence remaining at bench or simulation level.
watch_item: Evidence for graded Ti–hydroxyapatite interfaces came predominantly from non-DWBI analog studies, so device-specific performance remains unvalidated.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
